audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while the content layer reads Akshan/Akshan/Akshan then Cassiopeia x4. Two different answers render for every row.
audit.why: Content layer matches packet.levelChart exactly, and the reasoning holds: Akshan bullies a dashless mage at 1-3, and the lane flips at Petrifying Gaze (level 6) plus Twin Fang uptime. Win rate 50.31% over 652 games supports a lane that flips rather than one side owning it.
audit.corrected: Full side rows set to Akshan, Akshan, Akshan, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia to match win[0..6] and the packet.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 phase text is garbled ('Avengerang... no —') and names Akshan's R 'Vengeance'. Content repeatedly calls Cassiopeia's ultimate 'Petrify'.
audit.why: Akshan's R is Comeuppance (100/85/70s, 2500 range). Cassiopeia's R is Petrifying Gaze (120/100/80s, 825 range) — it stuns only enemies facing her and slows those with their back turned, which is the actual level 6 spike in this lane.
audit.corrected: Real names used, with the facing mechanic and the 120s rank-1 cooldown stated so the dive timing is concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: MAJOR FABRICATION: the content layer credits Cassiopeia with 'Noxious Trap' and describes 'trap fields', 'traps everywhere', and 'her Trap placement'. Cassiopeia has no traps in her kit — that is a Teemo ability. Her zoning tool is Miasma (W), the grounding cloud.
audit.why: Kit file: Q Noxious Blast (3.5s, 850), W Miasma (24/22/20/18/16s, 700, grounds and slows), E Twin Fang (0.75s, 700, heals her, extra damage on poisoned targets), R Petrifying Gaze. The decisive interaction the page never states: Miasma GROUNDS, and grounded means Heroic Swing does not cast at all — she can shut off both your entry and your exit with one 24-second spell. Second decisive interaction, flagged in missingInteractions: Twin Fang heals her off every tick of chip damage, so Grievous Wounds decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Trap language removed everywhere. Miasma grounding stated as the swing-denial, with its rank-1 24s cooldown as the commit window. Anti-heal against Twin Fang promoted into breakdown.carry.
sources: enemyKit W text ('Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities')
enemyKit E text ('heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt')

audit.why: report[8] already carries 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain', which is right for Twin Fang. Left alone.

edits.after: Petrifying Gaze's 825-range stun and Twin Fang's 0.75s cycle make her a brutal late-game mage, and unless you execute her with Comeuppance before she sets up, long fights favour her hard.

edits.before: Cassiopeia has no dash and low base damage before she can lay traps everywhere, so you walk her down at levels 1-2 with E-Q combos and punish any trade attempt. Her Noxious Trap takes time to blanket the lane, and until then you can freely contest CS and poke. Respect her mana costs early — she can't spam Twin Fang forever without going dry.
edits.after: Cassiopeia has no dash and low base damage before she stacks levels, so you walk her down at 1-2 with swing-and-Q strings and punish any trade attempt. Miasma is a 24-second cooldown at rank 1, and once it is spent she cannot ground your E, so that is your window to contest CS and poke. Respect her mana — Twin Fang costs 40 a cast and drains her.

edits.before: This is where it flips: once she hits 6, Petrify's stun-if-facing mechanic turns any misstep into a full burst combo that outpaces your kit, and her passive move speed lets her kite your engages. Play around her trap fields carefully, and don't commit R into her unless you're sure she's already used Petrify. From here she's building toward a poke-and-burst lane state you can't out-trade head-on.
edits.after: This is where it flips: once she hits 6, Petrifying Gaze stuns anyone facing her and turns one misstep into a full Twin Fang burst, while Serpentine Grace amplifies every move speed buff she buys. Walk clear of Miasma before you swing — grounded, your E does not cast at all — and hold Comeuppance until her 120-second ultimate is spent. From here she out-trades you head-on.

edits.before: Cassiopeia's Twin Fang stacking damage and long-range Petrify stun make her a lane-phase and skirmish nightmare late — she deletes anyone she catches facing her. Your best plan is picking her off in side lane before objectives with R rather than fighting her in extended trades. If she groups with even one peel, avoid diving in without vision on her Trap placement.
edits.after: Cassiopeia's Twin Fang uptime and her 825-range Petrifying Gaze make her a skirmish nightmare late — she deletes anyone she catches facing her. Your best plan is executing her in the side lane with Comeuppance before objectives rather than trading with her. If she has peel, do not swing in: Miasma grounds the exit as surely as the entry, and you are left standing in the poison.

notes: This matchup carried a fabricated ability: 'Noxious Trap' (a Teemo ability) appeared in spikes[0] and the trap fiction spread through early, mid, late and wants.foe[0]. Cassiopeia has no traps; her zoning is Miasma. All trap language removed. Her ultimate was written as 'Petrify' throughout — corrected to Petrifying Gaze. The grounding interaction (Miasma disables Heroic Swing entirely, both in and out) was never stated anywhere on the page and is now in mid and late. Anti-heal versus Twin Fang, flagged in missingInteractions, is now in breakdown.carry as well as report[8].
